## TL;DR
Human-assigned tasks now get a `## Step-by-step guide` requirement: PM and engineer prompts demand it, `repoos new`/`update`/the API warn when it is missing, the scaffold includes the heading, and `repoos update --section` edits it alone. This round makes every markdown scan share one closure-aware fence mask.

## Work and rationale
- `src/core/markdown-fence.ts`: `markdownFenceMask` now treats a fence opener with no matching close before EOF as plain text, so one stray fence can no longer hide every later heading (pass-7 finding). `markdownFenceOpen` follows CommonMark (a backtick info string cannot contain a backtick).
- `src/core/task.ts`: `sectionStart`, `nextSection` and `collectActivityEntries` all use the mask, so `extractSection`, `replaceSection` and `removeSection` behave as on main for unbalanced bodies and still ignore fenced headings.
- `src/core/task-underspecified.ts` (`bundleSpecSections`, `extractHumanTaskGuideSection`) and `src/core/task-summary.ts` (`visibleSummaryLines`) use the same mask instead of their own scanners.
- Tests in `src/core/task-section-fence.test.ts`, including an unclosed fence before a section for extract, replace and remove.
- Earlier rounds on the branch: warning logic, scaffold, prompts, docs, drawer banner.

## Approaches tried
One shared mask rather than a fifth per-function scanner, since each review pass found the next copy of the same class.

## Challenges and blockers
Five unrelated `src/core` tests fail under bare vitest in this worktree (attachment-migration, canary, git-maintenance-lsof, task-dependencies); they are environment-sensitive and untouched by this diff.

## Key learnings
Fence-aware scanning needs a lookahead for closure; a state machine that only tracks "open" leaks past a stray opener.
